name: NIS Management Ltd
title: NIS Management Ltd - 544495 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: NIS Management Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose 13.96% to INR180.03 crore; FY26 PAT hit by INR27.82 crore labour-code provision, adjusted PAT INR19.12 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total income was INR180.03 crore (up 13.96% YoY), with EBITDA of INR11.11 crore (up 29.75%) and margin of 9.41% (up 115 bps). FY26 consolidated income was INR436.70 crore (up 7.74%) and EBITDA INR33.53 crore (up 12.19%, margin 7.68%, up 30 bps). Reported profitability absorbed a one-time, non-cash exceptional provision of INR27.82 crore for the new Labour Codes; adjusted FY26 PAT was INR19.12 crore and adjusted Q4 PAT INR6.86 crore. Management guided to 12-15% consolidated growth and a target of crossing INR500 crore in FY27.

segments.name: Security services
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at INR199.49 crore, 46.03% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Integrated FM, electronic security and CCTV rentals
segments.commentary: INR56.91 crore, 13.31% of revenue. CCTV was about INR12 crore, of which about INR7 crore was rental, generating roughly INR4 crore EBITDA.

segments.name: Other (course fees, allied receipts)
segments.commentary: INR5.99 crore in FY26. Keertika Academy revenue fell from about INR4 crore to INR2 crore as DDU-GKY projects ended; Education Associates LLP flat at about INR4 crore.

segments.name: NIS Facility Management Services (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell from about INR20 crore to INR16 crore as low-margin housing-society security contracts were exited. Standalone NIS Management grew about 10%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 12-15%, based on current order book plus in-year wins.
Management targets crossing INR500 crore consolidated revenue within FY26-27 timeframe (per call; target stated as 'within this financial year') and sees possible upside.
Expects CCTV revenue to pick up toward year end, with tenders in the next 2-3 months and 3-4 months of project work; AMC contracts expected to add margin.
Expects DDU-GKY Odisha project by June; Maharashtra and West Bengal DDU-GKY bids still under evaluation.
Plans to deploy the unutilised IPO proceeds (INR36.91 crore unutilised) significantly this year and fully within two years.
Management said it will not pursue growth that would compromise operating cash flow or margins.
capex_capacity: Operates across 14 states via 14 branches, 18,000+ personnel and more than 1,500 client sites.
CCTV revenue was flat in FY26 due to STQC Make-in-India certification, causing camera stock-outs.

New contracts: Haldia Dock (about INR50 lakh per month, three years), Reliance Gujarat (about 150 stores, about INR1 crore), Patna Secretariat (about INR1 crore per year for three years), West Bengal Irrigation Department (about INR1 crore for one year), NBDD (about INR10 lakh billing).
HDFC Bank branch additions, plus IndusInd and ICICI Bank additions in North India, add about INR10 crore per month in total.
Government CCTV work: Webel/New Town Smart City (INR56 lakh), Mumbai Police CCTV project (INR1 crore), Patna Secretariat housekeeping (INR10.36 crore over five years).
demand_pricing: Management expects West Bengal government tenders to lift business after the change in government; 2-3 more work orders expected from New Town Smart City and the electricity board.
Security market growing about 10-11% YoY; company says it is growing at 12-13%.
Labour-code wage pass-through: all contract labour costs, minimum wage hikes, PF, ESIC, leave and gratuity are passed through to clients, with no renegotiation demands yet.
West Bengal accounts for about 70-75% of business; draft labour-code rules from the state government are still awaited.
Largest clients: Reliance Retail about INR30 crore (INR35-36 crore expected FY27), DTET about INR24 crore, airport INR22-23 crore, HDFC Bank about INR19 crore, Anjali Jewellers INR12-13 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 revenue growth muted, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone grew about 10% as major contracts came in H2 (Haldia Dock, Reliance Gujarat) with little time to convert. Subsidiary revenue fell due to CCTV stock-outs, exits from low-margin housing-society contracts and delayed West Bengal projects; Keertika Academy fell about INR2 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are trade receivables high at about INR145 crore and what is the aging?
qa_highlights.answer: NIS Management debtors rose from INR107 crore (H1 start) to INR119 crore in H1 and INR124 crore by year-end, due to collection delays at Haldia Dock, Reliance Gujarat, Patna Secretariat and Irrigation. Debtors were about INR120 crore in April after collections; over 180 days is about INR5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Has the West Bengal election changed renewals, payments or tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: No impact on wins: a New Secretariat renewal came from PWD and a Webel CCTV order was won. DTET payments were delayed for April and May due to vote-on-account funding, though April was collected.

qa_highlights.question: Is there FY27 revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided 12-15% consolidated growth from the order book plus in-year wins. The MD cited a target of over INR500 crore in FY27 against INR436 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much annual revenue was lost from contracts ended or not renewed?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 revenue was about INR373 crore against INR352 crore in FY24 standalone, as Calcutta Airport (about INR15 crore a year) and IIT Bhubaneswar (INR6-7 crore) were lost. No renewals fell due in FY26; Calcutta Airport re-bid is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the labour-code impact on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contract labour costs are passed through to clients, and no client has sought renegotiation yet. Formalisation may cut informal operators' margins while expanding opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth not 30-40% given the small base?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD said faster growth is possible but low-margin, extended-credit tenders would hurt margins, cash flow and DSO. The company wants margins from most contracts before accelerating.

qa_highlights.question: Why are IPO proceeds not fully deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: INR36.91 crore is unutilised. New contracts started only from November to January after the September IPO, and about INR10 crore was deployed and recovered, so full deployment is expected within two years.

qa_highlights.question: When will CCTV revenue rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects better CCTV returns toward year end, with tenders in 2-3 months and 3-4 months of project work, plus AMC contracts for higher margin within about six months.

risks_watch: Receivables of about INR145 crore (about 33% of FY26 revenue) and collection delays from government clients such as DTET and Haldia Dock.
Pending West Bengal draft labour-code rules, which could affect wage and compliance costs for the 70-75% of business in that state.
EBITDA margin mix risk: security and housekeeping run at about 4.5-4.8% EBITDA, while higher-margin CCTV and IFM are stagnant.
Keertika Academy and DDU-GKY tenders for Maharashtra and West Bengal remain under evaluation.
Calcutta Airport re-bid and government renewals (New Secretariat, Nabanna) due next year.
Deployment of INR36.91 crore unutilised IPO proceeds.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the West Bengal government pipeline and on CCTV recovery, but cautious on growth pace, citing margin and cash-flow discipline. Answers on receivables and the IPO were detailed, and some were hard to follow; the CFO and MD were occasionally evasive on FY27 guidance.
key_quotes: So we are slightly shy of really increasing revenue without a very strong consideration towards the bottom line either in the terms of the margin or even the cash flow.
And we would not want a situation where our operating cash flow, especially free cash flow, going below what it is today.
This impact i s non -cash, accounting -led and transitionary in nature, reflecting alignment with statutory obligations.
So we should be crossing INR500 crores within this financial year.

adds.what: HDFC Bank branch additions plus IndusInd and ICICI Bank additions in North India, adding about INR10 crore per month in total (service contracts, not owned plan

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 12-15% (midpoint 13.5%) and a INR500 crore target, backed by the current order book (e.g., Haldia Dock, Reliance Gujarat, Patna Secretariat contracts) and in-year wins, but no owned capacity expansion was detailed and the INR500 crore target lacks specific timing beyond 'within FY27'.
